title: Monthly Account Invoice Rules for the Bluegate Business Storage Account
content:
The Bluegate Business Storage Account is billed by one monthly account invoice. These rules govern what that invoice carries, when it is issued, and how rents and business center services appear on it.

## Rules

**R1 — Invoice date and contents.** The account is invoiced on the first day of each calendar month; that day is the invoice date. The invoice carries the program's monthly program fee and the service charges of the previous calendar month.

**R2 — Delivery and purchase orders.** The invoice is delivered by the program's invoice delivery channel. A purchase-order number is printed on it where the program supports purchase-order numbers.

**R3 — Consolidated rents.** Where the program provides consolidated invoicing, the business's unit and parking rents are presented on the same invoice, each rent still booked on its own agreement's ledger.

**R4 — Rent volume discount.** The program's rent volume discount percentage applies to the monthly rent of each business-billed agreement while the business's count of active agreements is at least the program's volume discount threshold. The count is the number of the business's storage unit and parking agreements whose status is active, delinquent or moving out, taken at the date of handling. The percentage is taken off each agreement's own monthly rent.

**R5 — One invoice per month.** Each month is invoiced once: an account has at most one monthly invoice for a given invoice month.

**R6 — Business center services.** Conference room hours used beyond the program's included hours are charged at the program's conference room hourly fee. Forklift time is charged at the program's forklift fee for each started hour, where the program includes forklift service. Each authorized user added after the account opened is charged the program's fee per added authorized user.

**R7 — Account balance.** The account balance is what the business owes on its account invoices: program fees and service charges increase it; payments and credits decrease it.

## Worked invoice (hypothetical)

*All figures below are hypothetical inputs chosen for illustration; they are not any program's rates.* A program with a monthly program fee of $40.00, 3 included conference room hours at $12.00 an hour beyond them, forklift service at $45.00 a started hour, a fee of $10.00 per added user, and a rent volume discount of 5% from 3 active agreements.

During April the business used the conference room for 5 hours, used the forklift for 1 hour 10 minutes and added one authorized user. It holds 3 active agreements, two of them storage units at $200.00 a month each billed through the account.

| Line on the invoice dated 1 May | Basis | Amount |
|---|---|---|
| Monthly program fee | Program fee for May | $40.00 |
| Conference room, April | 5 hours used less 3 included, that is 2 hours at $12.00 | $24.00 |
| Forklift service, April | 1 hour 10 minutes is 2 started hours, at $45.00 | $90.00 |
| Authorized user added, April | 1 user at $10.00 | $10.00 |
| Account charges on this invoice | Total of the lines above | $164.00 |
| Unit rent, agreement 1 (presented) | $200.00 less 5%, booked on that agreement's ledger | $190.00 |
| Unit rent, agreement 2 (presented) | $200.00 less 5%, booked on that agreement's ledger | $190.00 |

The $164.00 increases the account balance. Each $190.00 rent is presented on the invoice but booked on its own agreement's ledger. Had the business held only 2 active agreements, the count would fall short of the threshold of 3 in this example and each rent would be presented at $200.00.
